To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) an algorithm that uses WordNet to provide glosses for Lesk's dictionarybased word sense disambiguating algorithm is effective, and (2) the use of WordNet's hypernymy relations in conjunction with glosses improves the accuracy of Lesk's algorithm over the use of glosses alone.
our adapted version of Lesk's algorithm, when applied to the English lexical sample from Senseval-2, attains an overall disambiguation accuracy of 32%.
the use of WordNet as a source of glosses in a Lesk algorithm improves performance over the standard Lesk algorithm, and that this improvement is statistically significant.

the application of a dictionary-based approach to the task of word sense disambigation.
the development of a word sense disambigation algorithm that is based on the Lesk algorithm.
the development of a new approach to word sense disambigation that is based on the semantic relations between words in the lexical database Wordnet.

our approach is a promising alternative to the standard Lesk algorithm, and is competitive with other approaches to word sense disambigation.

the use of WordNet in conjunction with a Lesk-based algorithm can provide a simple and effective word sense disambiguating system.
the adaptation of the Lesk's algorithm to WordNet provides a simple, yet effective method for WSD.
